data.description:
## Context / Problem

The `PreToolUse:Bash` hook fails intermittently with

    PreToolUse:Bash hook error
    Failed with non-blocking status code: /bin/sh: scripts/hooks/serena_grep_reminder.py: No such file or directory

The failure is non-blocking, so tool calls still run — but the Serena-vs-grep navigation guidance the
hook exists to inject is SILENTLY ABSENT for those calls, which is the whole point of the hook.

## Root cause — established by construction, not inferred

`.claude/settings.json` configures the hook with a RELATIVE command path:

    "matcher": "Bash",
    "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "scripts/hooks/serena_grep_reminder.py" }]

A relative command is resolved against the SHELL'S CURRENT WORKING DIRECTORY at hook time, not
against the project root. So the hook works or fails depending purely on where the preceding tool
call left the shell.

MEASURED on this host:

    MISSING  /Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.tickets-tracker
    PRESENT  /Users/joeoakhart/feat-c403-overlap-batch
    PRESENT  /Users/joeoakhart/fix/1157-ladder-windows
    PRESENT  /Users/joeoakhart/feat/0d76-bedrock-parity

`.tickets-tracker` is the ticket store — a separate git worktree with no `scripts/` directory. Any
Bash call issued while the shell sits there fails the hook. That matches the observed occurrences
exactly: the errors appeared in a run immediately after ticket-store commands, which leave the shell
cwd in `.tickets-tracker`.

This is not a missing file. The script is present and executable in the main checkout and in every
code worktree checked; only the resolution path is wrong.

## Why it matters more than a cosmetic warning

* It fails OPEN and QUIET. The guidance simply does not appear, and nothing in the transcript says
  "you are now operating without the navigation reminder" — an agent cannot tell a call that got the
  hint from one that did not.
* It is CWD-dependent, so it is intermittent and looks flaky. That invites the wrong diagnosis
  ("transient hook error") instead of the real one.
* It affects any repo-adjacent working directory, not just `.tickets-tracker` — any tool call run
  from `/tmp`, a scratch dir, or a non-repo path hits the same thing.

## Approach

Make the command path independent of the caller's cwd. Claude Code exposes `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` for
exactly this, so the command should be `"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/scripts/hooks/serena_grep_reminder.py"`
(quoted). An absolute path would also work but is not portable across checkouts, and this repo is
routinely used from multiple worktrees, so the project-dir form is preferable.

Worth checking in the same pass whether any OTHER hook in `.claude/settings.json` uses a relative
command and has the same latent defect.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The hook resolves and runs from ANY working directory, including `.tickets-tracker` and a
      directory outside the repository entirely.
- [ ] A check or test asserts no hook in `.claude/settings.json` is configured with a relative command
      path, so the defect cannot silently return.
- [ ] Every other hook entry in the file is audited for the same relative-path issue and fixed or
      explicitly confirmed safe.
- [ ] Verified by running a Bash tool call with the shell cwd in `.tickets-tracker` and observing the
      hook's guidance appear rather than an error.
data.title: PreToolUse Bash hook uses a relative command path, so it silently fails from any cwd without scripts/
